content: Wild ginger refers to a genus of herbaceous plants known as Asarum, which belongs to the birthwort family, Aristolochiaceae. The species Asarum canadense is native to the forests of eastern North America. Its distribution extends from the Great Plains to the Atlantic Coast and from southeastern Canada southward to the fall line in the southeastern United States. Another species, Asarum caudatum, is found in British Columbia and extends southward through Washington and Oregon to central California, as well as from the Coast Range eastward to western Montana. The plant is commonly referred to as wild ginger because its rhizome has a taste and aroma similar to that of true ginger root, although the two are not closely related botanically. The rhizome can be used as a spice, but it also acts as a potent diuretic, stimulating urinary output. However, Asarum canadense and other species within the genus contain aristolochic acid, a chemical compound that has been shown to be carcinogenic in rats. The birthwort family, which includes the genus Aristolochia, is also known to contain human carcinogens. Wild ginger thrives in moist, shaded environments with humus-rich soil. The plant features deciduous, heart-shaped leaves that grow in opposite pairs and emerge from a rhizome located just beneath the soil surface. Each year, two new leaves grow from the rhizome's growing tip. The plant produces unique jug-shaped flowers, which are borne singly in the spring between the bases of the leaves. These flowers have earned the plant the alternative name little jug. Wild ginger is well-suited for cultivation in shade gardens and serves as an attractive ground cover. Species of Wild Ginger: Asarum arifolium Asarum canadense: Commonly known as Wild Ginger, Black Snakeroot, Canada Wild Ginger, Canadian Snakeroot, or Broad-leaved Asarabacca. Asarum caudatum: Known as Long-tailed Wild Ginger or British Columbia Wild Ginger. Subspecies include: Asarum caudatum caudatum: British Columbia Wild Ginger. Asarum caudatum viridiflorum: Long-tail Wild Ginger. Asarum europaeum: Also called Asarabacca, European Wild Ginger, Haselwort, or Wild Spikenard. Asarum hartwegii: Known as Hartweg's Wild Ginger. Asarum hongkongensis: Referred to as Hong Kong Wild Ginger. Asarum lemmonii: Known as Lemmon's Wild Ginger. Asarum marmoratum: Called Marbled Wild Ginger. Asarum naniflorum Asarum splendens: Commonly referred to as Chinese Wild Ginger.
